question: With the extra-inning runner on 2nd, does bunting the runner to 3rd pay, and has the home edge changed?
answer: There is no measurable edge either way. Visitors' bunts are worth -0.16 runs (CI -0.35 to +0.02). Home teams win 50.0% of extra games.
findings: Visitors, tied, a leadoff bunt try against swinging: runs -0.16 (CI -0.35 to +0.02), win -1.2 points (CI -9.3 to +6.5).
Home, tied, a bunt try against swinging: scored -0.3 points (CI -9.1 to +8.4), win +1.0 points (CI -6.1 to +7.8).
The home win % in extra-inning games was 51.4% in 2015-19 (n=1,003) and 50.0% in 2020-25 (n=1,125).
The leadoff bunt attempt rate in extras is 13.9% of 3,132 halves. Bunters hit -15 points of wOBA and swingers +4.
method: The leadoff PA of each extra half-inning (runner on 2nd, 0 out), non-pitchers. A bunt try is a bunt in play or a foul or missed bunt. A linear model with batter-season wOBA and season, with game bootstrap CIs. Intent beyond the batter isn't observed.
data: Retrosheet play-by-play, 2020-2025 regular season (7-inning games removed), 2,232 tied extra half-innings; 2015-19 extras for home win %. Retrosheet: the information used here was obtained free of charge from and is copyrighted by Retrosheet (www.retrosheet.org).
split_check: Win difference, bunt minus swing: visitors -9.8 points in 2020-22 and +1.9 in 2023-25, home +8.8, +0.4 (raw).
